Claim_Current_Wording: Short-term supplements should be evaluated on operational outcomes rather than biomarker surrogates.
Evidence_Result: 12 mg/day astaxanthin for four weeks produced no statistically or clinically significant cardiometabolic or fire-ground performance effect; most inflammatory changes were within treatment groups.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that astaxanthin improves occupational performance or cardiometabolic health in firefighters or Brazilian public safety.

Claim_Current_Wording: Military supplementation effects are heterogeneous and require outcome-specific appraisal.
Evidence_Result: Sixteen studies reported inconsistent and mostly modest performance/recovery findings; authors state there is inadequate practical evidence for field performance guidance.
Relevant_Location: Methods 2; Results 3 and Table 3; Limitations 4.4; Conclusions 5.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not justify a general supplementation protocol, causal field-readiness claim, or direct transfer to Brazilian public safety.

Claim_Current_Wording: In a small firefighter trial, creatine added to protein/carbohydrate was associated with improvement in selected task times.
Evidence_Result: Creatine group showed larger improvement in rescue (difference 1.78 s, 95% CI 0.61-2.95; p=.004) and forcible entry (2.66 s, 95% CI 0.68-4.65; p=.01), with no interaction for other tasks or total time.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that protein/carbohydrate alone caused benefit, that every occupational task improved, or that results generalize to female firefighters or Brazilian agencies.

Claim_Current_Wording: The 30-15 IFT showed reproducible cardiorespiratory-fitness estimates in one infantry cohort.
Evidence_Result: End-running speed, maximal heart rate and predicted VO2max test-retest ICCs were .971, .960 and .975; authors report validity/usefulness against treadmill and 2-mile run measures.
Relevant_Location: Methods: Study design and procedures; Results and Table 2; Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not validate the test for Brazilian policing, establish combat readiness, or prove outcome prediction beyond this small infantry cohort.

Claim_Current_Wording: Body armour can increase workload and impair selected physical-task outcomes; effects are outcome- and system-specific.
Evidence_Result: Across 16 eligible studies, authors report increased workload, lower work capacity, slower functional-task completion, impaired balance/stability and higher RPE; marksmanship and some physiological effects remain uncertain.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not quantify the effect of a particular Brazilian vest, prove injury prevention effects, or establish cognitive/marksmanship decrement in all settings.

Claim_Current_Wording: Automated positive feedback may improve selected implementation perceptions within a specific policing deployment.
Evidence_Result: In two Arizona departments (n=84 responses), adjusted probability of rating the platform appropriate was 21.7 percentage points higher in the feedback department (p=.011); feasibility was not significant.
Relevant_Location: Pilot 03: Setting; Tables 1-4; Limitations; Conclusion. FT1 digest: Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish improved officer behavior, public safety, accountability, technology accuracy, causal organization-wide benefit or Brazilian applicability.

Claim_Current_Wording: Selected US police leaders reported CFIR-aligned barriers and facilitators relevant to planning, not effectiveness.
Evidence_Result: Seventy-two respondents, mostly senior personnel, described innovation complexity, limited tailoring and low trust of external implementers; data are descriptive and convenience-sampled.
Relevant_Location: Pilot 03: Study population; Survey measures; Results/Table 3-5; Limitations. FT1 digest confirms Methods, Results and Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish prevalence across US policing, causal determinants of implementation success, innovation effectiveness or transferability to Brazil.

Claim_Current_Wording: Hydration monitoring proposals for firefighters require direct outcome evaluation before institutional adoption.
Evidence_Result: Review recommends multi-measure hydration assessment and notes no firefighter randomized trials demonstrating health effects of maintained euhydration.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that the suggested volumes or thresholds improve health, performance or safety in firefighters or Brazilian public safety.

Claim_Current_Wording: Long-running implementation portfolios can align program delivery, policy and research, subject to context-specific evaluation.
Evidence_Result: Describes WRAIR PEPFAR implementation-science protocols and institutional synergies, without a controlled operational-readiness comparison.
Relevant_Location: Full text: narrative synthesis; Tables 1-2; Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that a military HIV portfolio improves public-safety readiness or transfers to Brazil.

Claim_Current_Wording: Phase angle was associated with standardized physical-performance measures beyond DXA body composition in U.S. Marines.
Evidence_Result: In 2,177 Marines, PFT increased from 236 to 271 and CFT from 240 to 272 across standardized phase-angle muscle-quality quartiles; models retained sex covariates.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that phase angle causes performance or validates a Brazilian operational threshold.

Claim_Current_Wording: Police occupational-health nutrition strategies should be locally assessed rather than inferred from one cross-sectional survey.
Evidence_Result: Among 262 Polish officers, reported diet frequency patterns were suboptimal and excess adiposity common; no causal readiness outcome was tested.
Relevant_Location: Methods 2; Results 3 and Tables 1-3; Limitations 5; Conclusion 6.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish diet causes adiposity or readiness, nor describe Brazilian police prevalence.

Claim_Current_Wording: Stakeholders can identify feasible injury-prevention priority areas for police recruits before intervention testing.
Evidence_Result: Forty-eight participants generated, sorted and rated priorities; eight broad injury-prevention areas emerged from recruits, staff, clinicians and researchers.
Relevant_Location: Methods: concept mapping; Results: participants and Tables 1-4; Limitations; Conclusion.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that any mapped strategy prevents injury or transfers unchanged to Brazilian academies.

Claim_Current_Wording: Heat acclimation was associated with reduced rate-pressure product in the studied controlled protocol, with similar change magnitude by sex.
Evidence_Result: Twenty-seven volunteers completed ten heat-acclimation visits; rate-pressure product decreased from day 1 to day 10 under linear mixed models.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish sex-specific field readiness, safety, or performance benefit in police/firefighters.

Claim_Current_Wording: mTBI recovery requires multidisciplinary consideration, while return-to-duty interventions require direct outcome evidence.
Evidence_Result: Narrative review identifies multidisciplinary recovery domains and a proposed holistic performance framework.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not demonstrate effectiveness of holistic programming or a validated return-to-duty pathway.

Claim_Current_Wording: Tactical police medic practice is shaped by competence, regulations, interagency coordination and tactical demands.
Evidence_Result: Interviews identify constraints on civilian care, inconsistent healthcare cooperation and ethical/operational dilemmas for Swedish tactical police medics.
Relevant_Location: Full text: methods/interviews; themes; Limitations; Conclusions.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not measure patient outcomes, validate training duration or justify a Brazilian scope-of-practice policy.

Claim_Current_Wording: Vision-related health risks may warrant context-specific occupational-health review in visually demanding roles.
Evidence_Result: Review outlines military ocular-hypertension detection barriers and suggested strategies; no tested screening effect on readiness is reported.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not demonstrate glaucoma prevalence, screening effectiveness or readiness impact in Brazilian public safety.

Claim_Current_Wording: Musculoskeletal symptom burden can be high in tactical police units and warrants ergonomic/organizational assessment.
Evidence_Result: 255 officers reported 92.9% 12-month MSD prevalence; multi-site symptoms were common, but associations are cross-sectional.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish occupational load causes MSDs or estimate Brazilian prevalence.

Claim_Current_Wording: Injury surveillance may inform recovery planning for military trainees.
Evidence_Result: 109 male cadets with diagnosed stress fractures were described; tibia predominated and most were managed conservatively.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not estimate population incidence, establish prevention effectiveness or transfer to Brazilian police academies.

Claim_Current_Wording: TCCC training design should be evaluated by competence and outcomes rather than presumed learning-style fit.
Evidence_Result: 61 participants differed descriptively in Kolb learning-style distributions; authors state no educational effectiveness outcome was assessed.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that tailoring to learning styles improves TCCC competence or patient outcomes.

Claim_Current_Wording: NR — NOT REPORTED
Evidence_Result: Clinical surgical recovery comparisons in 64 servicemen do not address operational-readiness framework claims.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that a procedure improves operational readiness or justify public-safety treatment policy.

Claim_Current_Wording: NR — NOT REPORTED
Evidence_Result: Exploratory COMT/ACE associations are not a decision-ready operational assessment.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not support genetic screening, resilience prediction or causal performance claims.

Claim_Current_Wording: Officers describe organizational and cultural barriers that can delay injury care.
Evidence_Result: Seven interviews generated themes on athletic-trainer roles, injury management, stigma and administrative barriers.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show athletic trainers reduce injury burden or improve readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: Sleep telehealth implementation can be evaluated using uptake, symptom, monitoring and stakeholder outcomes.
Evidence_Result: 270 participants used a platform with app/wearable monitoring; implementation outcomes were mapped to RE-AIM, with mixed stakeholder data.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish operational readiness, comparative clinical effectiveness or Brazilian system feasibility.

Claim_Current_Wording: Tactical contexts impose nutrition and recovery constraints distinct from conventional sport settings.
Evidence_Result: Narrative synthesis adapts sport nutrition principles; it does not provide a pooled tactical-effect estimate.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish the stated dose guidance as effective in Brazilian operational forces.

Claim_Current_Wording: Military aviation fatigue countermeasures require operational validation and cannot rely on a single approach.
Evidence_Result: The article narrates short-term pharmacological findings but does not expose sufficient review methods or study-level evidence for a stronger claim.
Relevant_Location: Abstract; conclusion; methods/results reported as NR.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not justify stimulant policy, safety claims, or causal operational-readiness effects.

Claim_Current_Wording: Higher graduation-stage fitness was associated with better first-year supervisor-rated performance and lower musculoskeletal-injury hazard in one Chinese police academy cohort.
Evidence_Result: Among 216 followed recruits, each one-point composite fitness increase was associated with HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.83-0.95) for injury; BARS association beta=0.21 (95% CI 0.12-0.30).
Relevant_Location: Methods; Results/Table 1 and regression results; Limitations.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not prove that fitness testing, assignment, or conditioning causes lower injury or better performance.

Claim_Current_Wording: In young Chinese male military personnel, higher stress scores correlated with greater attention to negative information and expressive inhibition, and lower positive attention and cognitive reappraisal.
Evidence_Result: N=673; stress correlated with negative attention r=0.335 and expressive inhibition r=0.269, and inversely with positive attention r=-0.159 and cognitive reappraisal r=-0.162 (all p<0.001); resilience correlation was not significant.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish psychological mechanisms, mediation, intervention effects, or readiness improvement.

Claim_Current_Wording: Small exploratory data indicate that low or suboptimal energy availability and short sleep can co-occur among female ROTC cadets.
Evidence_Result: Four of ten met the study LEA threshold and five more were suboptimal; only two met the Army sleep recommendation.
Relevant_Location: Methods; Results energy availability and sleep sections.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not estimate prevalence in military women generally or prove that energy availability caused sleep or performance outcomes.

Claim_Current_Wording: Age and years in service were associated with cardiometabolic and physical-performance measures in one US career-firefighter department.
Evidence_Result: After adjustment, years of fire-service experience was associated with selected CVD-risk/body-composition and performance parameters; observational analyses cannot separate occupational exposure from ageing.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that fire service accelerates ageing or that monitoring changes operational outcomes.

Claim_Current_Wording: In a small cadet crossover trial, pork- versus plant-based MREs altered some recovery biomarkers and soreness measures, while ACFT performance differences were mostly absent.
Evidence_Result: N=23; no treatment-by-time interaction for overall performance (p=0.811); several recovery measures favoured pork, while plant diet had a faster two-mile run at one comparison (p=0.006).
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish long-term dietary superiority, operational effectiveness, or a universal MRE policy.

Claim_Current_Wording: NR — NOT RELEASED
Evidence_Result: Strength/power predicted simulated task time (adjusted R2=0.436), whereas the model did not predict cognitive errors; participants were non-firefighters.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish occupational readiness effects in firefighters.

Claim_Current_Wording: In one male firefighter department, resilience correlated with lower anxiety, depression, and PTSD symptom scores; most fitness outcomes had no association with psychological scores.
Evidence_Result: Resilience accounted for variance in trait anxiety (41.0%), state anxiety (25.4%), depression (20.5%), and PCL-5 (7.0%); only depression related to push-ups (p=0.014).
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that resilience training improves mental health or physical fitness.

Claim_Current_Wording: Australian infantry trainees described schedule, food-access, and self-efficacy barriers to performance nutrition.
Evidence_Result: Ten completers reported energy intake at 46% and 53% of estimated requirements in weeks 1 and 17; focus-group themes identified time and food-access barriers.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not estimate population intake or show that an education/access intervention changes readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: A Polish defence-sector sample had substantial calculated cardiovascular risk and limited risk-factor awareness.
Evidence_Result: Of 196 participants (153 soldiers), 66.3% had moderate and 21.4% high POL-SCORE risk; the sample also included 43 civilian employees.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish prevalence in armed forces or that screening improves operational readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: Spanish aeronautical military personnel had low carbohydrate and several micronutrient intakes relative to cited recommendations.
Evidence_Result: N=390 males; 83.8% were below carbohydrate guidance, while 98% were below vitamin-D and 76.6% below iodine recommendations.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish deficiency by biomarker, performance impairment, or effectiveness of dietary intervention.

Claim_Current_Wording: Hazardous alcohol-screen scores were associated with selected cardiometabolic risk markers in a large firefighter sample.
Evidence_Result: N=2,405; high AUDIT-C was associated with higher total cholesterol and blood pressure after stated adjustments, while VO2peak and peak power did not differ.
Relevant_Location: Methods; Results cardiometabolic and physical-capacity sections; limitations.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show alcohol use causes cardiometabolic changes or that screening/intervention improves readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: US Army body-composition standards have measurement and accession-versus-retention policy implications.
Evidence_Result: NHANES modelling found 29-50% of men and 39-50% of women failed current standards across age groups; results are not observed readiness outcomes.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not demonstrate that a specific body-composition standard improves readiness or applies to Brazil.

Claim_Current_Wording: In non-firefighter participants, acute aerobic or resistance exercise did not alter cognitive-flexibility errors during a subsequent simulated occupational task.
Evidence_Result: N=29; total, perseverative, and non-perseverative errors did not differ by condition (all p>0.39); aerobic exercise lowered one HRV frequency-domain measure.
Relevant_Location: Methods participants/procedure; Results WCST and HRV sections.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish on-shift exercise effects in firefighters or broader cognitive readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: Simulation fidelity can be evaluated with workload and situation-awareness measures.
Evidence_Result: N=10; NASA-TLX workload did not differ significantly between simulation settings.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish combat-readiness improvement from simulation fidelity.

Claim_Current_Wording: Post-deployment mental-health and alcohol screening can identify concurrent readiness-relevant burden.
Evidence_Result: Among 150 UPDF soldiers, 24 screened positive for PTSD (16%); results are screening data, not clinical diagnosis or causal effects.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish alcohol or PTSD causes reduced combat readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: Dietary patterns and cardiovascular-risk measures can be jointly assessed in firefighter wellness programs.
Evidence_Result: Career firefighters completed dietary and health assessments; observational associations do not determine dietary causation.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that diet modification changes cardiovascular risk or readiness.

Claim_Current_Wording: Short training interruption can be monitored with cardiorespiratory and strength measures.
Evidence_Result: Four weeks of detraining did not significantly alter several anthropometric or isometric-strength outcomes in this small sample.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not quantify a general detraining effect or justify readiness policy.

Claim_Current_Wording: Body-composition standards may have performance and health trade-offs requiring cautious assessment.
Evidence_Result: Review scope addresses body composition, performance and health but no extractable pooled effect was reported.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish a body-composition threshold or causal readiness effect.

Claim_Current_Wording: Mild-to-moderate COVID-19 may be followed with occupational cardiorespiratory testing in firefighters.
Evidence_Result: Records identified 152 reported infections; two hospitalization cases were excluded, so findings apply only to the retained mild-to-moderate cohort.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish COVID-19 caused changes in all firefighters or set return-to-duty thresholds.

Claim_Current_Wording: HRV feasibility can be explored during specialist-police selection, but predictive utility remains uncertain.
Evidence_Result: N=6; five candidates withdrew and one completed the two-day course.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not validate HRV for selection or attrition prediction.

Claim_Current_Wording: Low energy availability and poor sleep can co-occur in male ROTC cadets.
Evidence_Result: N=13; mean energy availability was 28.3 kcal/kg FFM, 62% met the study low-EA threshold and none reached optimal EA.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not estimate prevalence in military personnel or prove energy availability causes sleep/readiness effects.

Claim_Current_Wording: In one Midwest police department, body-composition, activity and strength measures were examined in relation to occupational-readiness-assessment performance.
Evidence_Result: N=30 incumbent officers; cross-sectional analysis relates measured characteristics to a Physical Readiness Assessment.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not show that modifying activity or body composition causes performance change.

Claim_Current_Wording: Circumference-based estimates may not accurately track body-fat change during basic combat training compared with DXA.
Evidence_Result: N=1,407 trainees had pre/post DXA and circumference data over eight weeks of BCT.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that DXA-based monitoring improves readiness or applies to non-US settings.

Claim_Current_Wording: A firefighter return-to-work task battery can be assessed for rating reliability before its use in screening.
Evidence_Result: Forty-two volunteers enrolled and 35 completed both online rating sessions; study evaluates rater reliability.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish that the screen predicts safe return to duty.

Claim_Current_Wording: Anaerobic-fitness and mental-toughness measures can be explored in relation to firefighter physical-ability-test time.
Evidence_Result: N=14 male firefighters completed PAT and anaerobic/mental-toughness measures.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not validate a predictive selection or readiness model.

Claim_Current_Wording: Marine body composition varies across high-performing roles.
Evidence_Result: Descriptive US Marine Corps body-composition findings.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal or threshold inference.

Claim_Current_Wording: Tactical strength-and-conditioning programs can be feasibility-tested with firefighters.
Evidence_Result: TARP reports feasibility outcomes, not definitive effectiveness.
Prohibited_Inference: No definitive operational-performance claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Tactical-athlete nutrition recommendations require context-specific implementation.
Evidence_Result: Position stand synthesizes nutrition considerations.
Prohibited_Inference: Not direct evidence of Brazilian operational effect.

Claim_Current_Wording: Body composition and selected biomarkers were associated with ACFT performance.
Evidence_Result: Associational ACFT analysis; no causal intervention tested.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal supplement or screening claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Cognitive resilience can be experimentally assessed under psychological stress.
Evidence_Result: Study examines cognitive responses to stress.
Prohibited_Inference: No broad readiness-effect inference.

Claim_Current_Wording: Sex, occupation and rank were associated with ACL-injury risk in tactical athletes.
Evidence_Result: Retrospective cohort reports risk associations.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal or prevention-effect claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Cardiorespiratory fitness was examined in relation to physiological response and dropout during loaded marching.
Evidence_Result: Cohort evaluates march response and dropout.
Prohibited_Inference: No universal fitness threshold.

Claim_Current_Wording: NR — NOT REPORTED
Evidence_Result: Clinical TCCC review.
Prohibited_Inference: Not evidence for present readiness claims.

Claim_Current_Wording: Ankle-sprain recurrence can be quantified in military health-system data.
Evidence_Result: Five-year population-level cohort.
Prohibited_Inference: No prevention-effect claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Perceived healthy-eating barriers can be assessed in ROTC cadets.
Evidence_Result: Pilot associations, not intervention effects.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal nutrition claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Foam-rolling effects were tested on loaded military-task performance and perceived recovery.
Evidence_Result: Task-performance and recovery outcomes reported in a short intervention study.
Prohibited_Inference: No long-term readiness claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Body composition was evaluated in relation to post-exercise parasympathetic reactivation among firefighter recruits.
Evidence_Result: Associational recruit study.
Prohibited_Inference: No readiness or intervention effect.

Claim_Current_Wording: Police occupational categories showed body-composition differences.
Evidence_Result: Cross-sectional comparison with activity moderation.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal occupational inference.

Claim_Current_Wording: Career-firefighter nutrient intake can be compared with reference intakes.
Evidence_Result: Descriptive nutrient-intake comparison.
Prohibited_Inference: No performance or intervention effect.

Claim_Current_Wording: Vitamin-D status and depression were assessed in a tactical-athlete population.
Evidence_Result: Cross-sectional association.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal or supplementation claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: A firefighter exercise program was tested for simulated fire-ground performance, endurance and strength.
Evidence_Result: Pilot investigation reports training outcomes.
Prohibited_Inference: No definitive program-effect claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Physical workload exposure and musculoskeletal complaints were assessed in deployed Swedish soldiers.
Evidence_Result: Occupational exposure/complaint associations.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal workload or prevention claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Prospective risk factors for back pain were assessed in marines.
Evidence_Result: Prospective cohort reports risk factors.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal prevention claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Police sleep quality has been systematically reviewed.
Evidence_Result: Systematic-review/meta-analysis evidence, held provisional.
Prohibited_Inference: No Brazil-specific or causal organizational claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Work stress and sleep disorders in law enforcement were systematically reviewed.
Evidence_Result: Systematic-review/meta-analysis evidence, held provisional.
Prohibited_Inference: No causal or Brazil-specific claim.

Claim_Current_Wording: Muscle discomfort and lifestyle factors were assessed among Brazilian military police in administrative and tactical force roles.
Evidence_Result: Brazilian cross-sectional occupational findings.
Prohibited_Inference: Does not establish causal occupational effect or intervention benefit.
